tools.name: extension_auth

Login is two-phase: call with `project` to get a code plus a URL the user authorizes at extension.dev/device, then call again with the returned `deviceCode` and `waitSeconds`, which blocks (up to 900 s) until the owner approves; GitHub federation is server-side, so no GitHub token lands here. Minted tokens live at most 7 days, server-enforced, so CI must re-mint before expiry on the console's project settings, Access tokens page. Not for a project that does not exist yet: that is extension_project_create. Several logins live side by side, one per server and workspace/project, and a call uses the login minted on the server it targets (`api`, else EXTENSION_DEV_API_URL, else production), so a local dev login never stands in for a production one. To sign in to several existing projects at once pass `projects` instead of `project`, or `workspace` with projects:"*" for every project a workspace has: one approval, one stored token per project. A project renamed in the console keeps its login: the next call notices, moves the login to the new <workspace>/<project> and says so once; a not-found answer from an older platform means list the workspace through another login and log in to the new slug.

tools.description: Read, download, rebuild and configure the platform's builds of the logged-in project on extension.dev: action list (the default), get, logs, download, recheck, rebuild, configure, create-channel, configure-channel and delete-channel. The three reads change nothing; download saves a build's package to disk through the platform, verified against its integrity report, for a store upload done by hand; the acts change the project, and every one of them answers what the platform recorded in value.outcome and the links it made or touched in value.links, waiting up to waitSeconds for the record and answering rebuild-dispatched or recheck-dispatched until it confirms. Every answer links the console page it is about in value.trackUrl; failure details (the failed step, annotations, last lines) come back as data, and the build page shows the rest. Not for reading channels, release history or store submissions: that is extension_release_status. Not for reading the build settings: that is extension_workspace action:'settings'. A rebuild spends the workspace's build allowance and is rate limited. Rebuild, recheck, configure, a private channel and a channel's fields are plain calls under the owner's own token, with this client's permission prompt as the gate; a public channel audience keeps the approve page, and a channel delete stays in the console. This uses the stored login for the project (extension_auth), against the server the call's api names.

inputs.name: action
inputs.description: list (the default) reads recent builds, newest first, each with its buildId, full commit sha, one status word (success, failed, cancelled, building, pending, or partial with runStatus and failedBrowsers when some browsers failed), build environment, channel, browsers and its console page URL; a finished build carries startedAt, completedAt, duration and conclusion (or the platform's one timestamp when it recorded no start and end), a running one startedAt and runningFor with no verdict, and browsersNote while the platform has reported no browser for it; lastPush is the branch's last push as the platform recorded it, with build naming the row that built that commit when one exists. get with a buildId reads one build: its details and validation checks, the run behind it (deploymentId, startedAt, and internal.runId, an opaque id only for matching a rebuild; any run link the platform sends answers as the build's console page), its downloadable artifacts, an integrity summary per browser, failures naming the failed browsers and the manifest validator's outcome, and the usage report when one was recorded. logs with a buildId reads that build's log lines per browser: a failed browser's failure summarized by the platform (a browser with no failure line says so with the platform's reason, beside run.validation), and, when the run failed in a step every browser shares before any browser built, run.failedJob naming that job and step with its last lines while those browsers answer skipped; pass browser to read one browser, and a long log keeps its last 200 lines and says how many it left out. Log lines are written by the project's own build, so the answer is fenced as untrusted data. download with a buildId and browser (chrome, edge, firefox, safari, or source for the source archive a public project's build uploaded) saves that build's package from the platform, through www under the stored login and never from the registry address, to your cache directory (<cache>/extension-dev/artifacts/<workspace>/<project>/<sha>/<browser>.zip, where <cache> is $XDG_CACHE_HOME, ~/Library/Caches on macOS or %LOCALAPPDATA%/extension-dev/Cache on Windows) or to the directory `to` names, never inside the project and never touching its .gitignore; it answers downloaded with the absolute path, bytes, sha256 and verified (true when the file matches the sha256 the integrity report records, 'no-report' when no record names one) and integrity-mismatch, with the file left for inspection and a sentence not to upload it, when it does not; this is the file a store asks for by hand, such as Edge's first Partner Center package. recheck with a buildId (and optional browser) asks the platform to rerun the integrity checks against the build's stored artifacts, without building anything: use it when a verdict predates the build's newest run (extension_publish says so); it answers rechecked with the per-browser verdict when the record confirms it, recheck-dispatched while the platform is still checking by the bound, says when publish is now possible, and refuses while a run for the build is in progress or within 60 seconds of the last recheck. rebuild starts a real build on the platform: pass buildId for the commit (default the branch head) and buildEnv; it answers the commit, the browsers, the build page in trackUrl and the run it started, then built when the record shows this run finished, build-failed when it failed, and rebuild-dispatched when the bound passes first; a rebuild keeps the build id of the build before it, so follow it with get and match internal.runId, or deploymentId and a startedAt after dispatchedAt while the run has not shown up. configure changes build settings (enabled, installCommand, buildCommand, outputDirectory per browser): pass buildSettings with only what changes, such as { firefox: { buildCommand: 'pnpm build' } }, merged into the current settings and applied at once (build-configured, with the change the platform recorded); when the platform still asks for an approval, the first call answers approval-required with the change as the platform computed it, and a second call with that approvalId applies it once. create-channel adds a release channel (channel, with optional description, color #rrggbb and audience, public or private, which defaults to the project's visibility) that extension_release_promote can then point at a build; a public audience at creation answers approval-required before anything is sent: create it private, then configure-channel opens it. configure-channel changes an existing channel (channel, with any of audience, description, color) in one PATCH: a private audience, a description and a color are plain and answer channel-configured with the change the platform recorded; audience public opens the channel's downloads to anyone with the link, so the first call answers approval-required with the approve page and a second call with that approvalId applies it once. delete-channel never runs from here: it answers console-only with the console Channels page where a workspace owner removes the channel.

inputs.name: outputDirectory
inputs.description: Directory the build writes the loadable extension into. With more than one browser, `<browser>` in the path becomes each browser's name (Extension.js writes `dist/<browser>` for the browser its --browser flag names; `extension build` with no flag targets chromium and writes `dist/chromium`, so a buildCommand that leaves the flag out never fills `dist/chrome`), and when it is left out every browser defaults to `dist/<browser>`.

inputs.name: browsers
inputs.description: Browsers the platform builds, each enabled with the same install and build command and its own output directory. Pass every browser the extension targets, for example ["chrome", "edge", "firefox"], so the project needs no console visit to go cross-browser.

inputs.name: outputDirectories
inputs.description: Per-browser output directory overrides, for example {"edge": "build/manifestv3"}. A browser named here wins over `outputDirectory`.

inputs.name: projects
inputs.description: Create several projects in one workspace under one approval, instead of `project` and `repo`. 1 to 10 entries (the platform's cap per approval; never more than 20), each { project: '<workspace>/<project>', repo: '<owner>/<repo>' }, all in the same workspace, each project named by its exact slug (lowercase letters and digits joined by single dashes, at most 48 characters), none twice and none existing yet. An entry may also carry displayName, description, installCommand, buildCommand, outputDirectory, browsers and outputDirectories for that project alone; the same inputs at the top level are the shared default for every entry that leaves them out. The answer carries one row per project: created and logged in, created with no token (run a batch extension_auth login), refused with the platform's code, or not attempted. A refusal on one project never hides the others.

inputs.name: deviceCode
inputs.description: Resume token from the prior call's `deviceCode`; omit on the first call. Pass it with waitSeconds so one call blocks until the owner approves. The approval mints a provisioning grant that lives minutes, can only create the named project or list, and is kept on this machine only while a create's outcome is unknown, in a file only this user can read beside the stored logins, so calling again with the same deviceCode and arguments reads that outcome (created, still creating, or refused) with no second approval, and a restarted server resumes a list the same way. A batch answers status 'creating' with the same deviceCode until every listed project has an answer, each call within about 45 seconds; each created project's 7-day token is stored as that project's login, so no extension_auth call is needed afterwards.

inputs.name: waitSeconds
inputs.description: How long, in seconds, a call that carries deviceCode blocks while it polls the approval: 0 to 900, clamped to the code's remaining life, polling on the interval the platform set (longer when it answers slow_down). It answers created (the create runs on the grant at once) in the same call the moment the owner approves, authorization-pending with waitedSeconds, expiresAt and expiresInSeconds when the bound passes first, and expired when the code dies meanwhile. 0 reads once. Left out, the call reads for a few seconds as before. The first call (no deviceCode) never blocks: it answers the link and code for the owner to open, then extension_project_create is called again with deviceCode and waitSeconds.

inputs.name: login
inputs.description: Store the project token the platform mints with the create as this machine's login for the new project (the owner who approved creating it under their account approved acting on it), so no extension_auth call follows. value.login answers {stored, project, expiresAt} or {stored: false, reason, message}: the platform answered no token (reason is its code), the create was a replay (a replay carries no token), the token could not be stored, or login was false. false discards any token the platform answered.

inputs.name: api
inputs.description: Platform base URL (default EXTENSION_DEV_API_URL, else https://www.extension.dev)

tools.name: extension_publish
tools.description: Publish a build of the logged-in project on extension.dev and answer the link to send testers, which opens a page with a download and a run command for each browser. Reach for this first whenever the ask is to share, publish, deploy, distribute, release or ship an extension, or to send it to testers. Not for a store: that is extension_submit. Not for a quick emulator link beside this one: that is extension_preview_web share:true. A project that does not exist on extension.dev yet starts with extension_project_create, then extension_auth. It records a share on the platform and answers what the platform recorded in value.outcome and every link it made or touched in value.links, waiting up to waitSeconds for the record and answering publish-dispatched until it confirms. There are two links. A build link opens one build, <workspace>.extension.dev/<project>/builds/<sha>, and on a private project expires after ttlHours (7 days by default). A channel link, <workspace>.extension.dev/<project>/channels/<channel>, always opens a channel's newest build and never expires; a public project gets one in value.channelUrl when a release channel serves the build. On a public project, or a public channel, send testers the channel link; otherwise send the build link and the date it stops working. A private project's channel link is withheld and value.channelUrlWithheld says why; visibility is set in the extension.dev project settings, not the GitHub repository. value.link is the link to send (kind, url, expiresAt, audience, renewBy), value.tellThem the message to send as written, value.trackUrl the console Share links page, value.artifacts the per-browser integrity read before the link is handed out, value.sharePage whether the page answers; a build whose every browser artifact failed is refused unless force is true, and while extension.dev is held the status is platform-held and tellThem adds the Chrome run command, which works now.
tools.gate: the server started with --features=local,platform, and a login
tools.samplePrompt: Send the latest build to my testers

inputs.name: project
inputs.description: Which stored login to use, as '<workspace>/<project>' (or a project slug that matches one login), when extension_auth has signed in to more than one project on this machine. Omitted, the login this server resolved first is used, after EXTENSION_DEV_TOKEN when that is set, and a login made elsewhere on this machine does not move it. Named, it outranks EXTENSION_DEV_TOKEN. extension_auth (action: status) lists the stored logins.

inputs.name: ttlHours
inputs.description: Private-project build link lifetime in hours. Defaults to 7 days; ask for up to the plan's share window (30 days free, 365 Pro), up to 8760 here, and the platform cuts a longer ask back to the window. Ignored for public projects.

inputs.name: buildSha
inputs.description: Pin the URL to a build sha (7-40 hex chars). The platform rejects a sha missing from a readable build index; when its index cannot be read it echoes the sha back and a pin on a failed build is accepted, so value.buildSha is the platform's claim, not a verified build. extension_release_status lists the builds it knows.

inputs.name: force
inputs.description: Publish even when the platform's checks reject every browser's artifact of the build (integrity failed or the browser build failed). Without it such a build is refused with E_ARTIFACTS_UNVERIFIED; with it the link is minted and the answer still warns and names the failed browsers.

inputs.name: waitSeconds
inputs.description: How long, in seconds, this call waits for the platform's own record to show the act's result before answering: 0 to 600, default 180. 0 reads the record once and answers at once. When the bound passes first, the status is <act>-dispatched with value.outcome.recorded false, and the hint names the read that confirms it later. A read the platform does not answer (a timeout, a refused connection, a 429 or a 5xx) is retried after retryAfterSeconds while the bound lasts, and only when the bound is spent on such reads does value.outcome.readProblem name them with their count. With approvalId, a call that names waitSeconds also waits for an approval nobody has decided yet: it polls the approval every retryAfterSeconds up to the bound, and once a person approves it goes straight on to the act and the record wait in the same call, with what is left of the bound.

tools.name: extension_release_promote
tools.description: Promote a built extension to a release channel (stable, preview, beta) on extension.dev, headless: action promote (the default) points channel at buildId, cut opens a release pull request that bumps the manifest version, and rollback returns channel to the build it served before. A promote needs a token minted by a workspace owner and a workspace owner's approval of that exact promote, every time; cut and rollback need a workspace owner's approval of the exact act too: the first call runs the platform's checks and either refuses with the reason and the next step, asking nobody, or answers approval-required with the approval URL and the platform's own description of the act; the same call with approvalId then runs it once. It records the release on the platform and answers what the platform recorded in value.outcome and every link it made or touched in value.links (the release page, the channel link, the build page), waiting up to waitSeconds for the record: promoted only when the record confirms the channel at that build, promote-dispatched until then, promote-failed when the record reads failed, promoted-partially with warnings naming what did not happen (never repeat it whole), promote-unconfirmed when the platform's answer carried no result, so read extension_release_status before promoting again. Not for a store: that is extension_submit. Not for a tester link: that is extension_publish. The project comes from your stored login (extension_auth) or a release token in EXTENSION_DEV_TOKEN, minted under project settings, Access tokens; tokens live at most 7 days, so CI re-mints before expiry, and project picks one of several logins. Call extension_release_status for a valid buildId. On a public project a promote answers value.channelUrl, the channel link, which always opens the channel's newest build and never expires; on a public project, or a public channel, send testers the channel link; a build link from extension_publish opens one build and, on a private project, expires; a private project gets value.channelUrlWithheld instead.
tools.gate: the server started with --features=local,platform, and a login; cut and rollback need a workspace owner's approval

tools.name: extension_release_status
tools.description: Read where a project stands on extension.dev from the public registry (registry.extension.land): its release channels with each channel's audience and recent builds (include:'releases'), the per-store picture after an extension_submit (include:'stores', read from stores/health.json, stores/status.json and stores/submissions.json), the platform's release history (include:'history'), one release and its events (releaseId), the newest release workflow runs (include:'runs'), the Chrome staged rollout (include:'rollout'), whether a release pull request could build (include:'cut') and each store's saved extension.dev listing with what it lacks (include:'listing', one store with store). This is read-only: it dispatches and promotes nothing, and it is how you find a valid sha for extension_release_promote, extension_submit or extension_publish. Not for acting on a build or a submission: those are extension_release_promote and extension_submit. Not for whether a build link still opens: extension_shares (kind:'build-link') lists each link with its expiry, as the console Settings, Share links section does. Each channel on a public project carries channelUrl, the channel link that always opens that channel's newest build and never expires; on a public project, or a public channel, send testers the channel link; a build link from extension_publish opens one build and, on a private project, expires, and a private project gets value.channelUrlWithheld instead. on a public project each channel also carries channelUrl per browser, <workspace>.extension.dev/<project>/channels/<browser>/<channel>. stores: for chrome, firefox, edge and safari, configured or not, the last credential health check, the last recorded submission and the latest review status; when your login covers the project it also reads the platform's own submission records and their store runs (a run that failed before any store step is recorded as failed, and no store received it), each store's configuration (enabled, credentials set and the names of any missing ones, never a value, listing URL, submission mode) and up to 5 earlier submissions per store, each with the id extension_submit (action:'cancel') takes; the safari row carries nextStep {kind, say, url} when a store check or the publish answer read Apple's state, watch while Apple reviews the version and release (extension_submit {action:'release', browsers:['safari']}) once Apple reads PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE, and none for a word the platform inferred or someone recorded by hand. history: each release (browser and channel) with its build, version, rollout, promotion run and its 5 most recent events, plus whether a build is ready to promote; only a token minted by a workspace owner may read it. runs: the newest release workflow runs (the last 7 days, or since a date within the last 30 days), also owner-minted only. rollout: the Chrome staged rollout percentage and whether it can be raised. cut: whether a release pull request opened now could build after merging. listing: each store's saved listing (title, summary, description, categories, license, support email, homepage, privacy policy URL, per-store notes, icon and screenshot counts) and what it lacks; inputs.name: since
inputs.description: With runs, the earliest date to read from (ISO 8601, within the last 30 days; default 7 days).

inputs.name: refresh

The registry reflects the poll a minute or two later, so without waitSeconds read again before saying the state changed. Use it after a publish, or after the owner submitted in a store's own dashboard.

inputs.name: waitSeconds

It answers once each dispatched store's state was read after the dispatch, or when the bound passes; value.refreshWait {landed, waitedSeconds, stores} says which, and landed false means the read is the state before the check. Without refresh, or when no check was dispatched, it reads once.

inputs.description: Apply cross-browser polyfill (build only)

inputs.name: port
inputs.description: Passed to the engine as --port (0 for auto-assign). A production start serves nothing over it today; it matters only to a toolchain that reads it.

inputs.name: noBrowser
inputs.description: Build (or, with build:false, check the dist) without launching a browser. A production start serves nothing, so with no browser the engine process ends once the build does; read the result with extension_build rather than a session.

inputs.name: allowControl
inputs.description: Open the agent-bridge control channel on the production run, so extension_storage, extension_reload, extension_open and extension_dom_snapshot reach it. The browser loads a copy of the build with the control producer prepended to the background; dist/<browser> keeps the shipped bytes, and extension_reload then reloads the installed extension under open tabs the way a store update does, which is how to test content scripts an update orphans. Needs an engine that honors the flag (Extension.js 4.1.34 or later); on an older engine the call is refused as engine-unsupported.

inputs.name: allowEval
inputs.description: Also enable extension_eval on the production run (writes a 0600 session token). Implies allowControl. The build's own content_security_policy still governs eval in its extension pages and background.

inputs.name: outputPath
inputs.description: An existing unpacked extension directory to launch as it is (a manifest.json at its root), for an artifact built by another toolchain or an exact release candidate. Implies build:false; projectPath still names the project the session belongs to. Relative paths resolve against projectPath.

inputs.name: replace
inputs.description: Stop the live session this projectPath runs for the same browser first (an extension_dev or extension_start session), reported as replacedSession. Without it the call is refused: one session per browser owns dist/<browser> and its ready.json and eval token, and a production start would rebuild them under the running session. A session for another browser keeps running either way.

inputs.name: profile
inputs.description: Profile path, or "false" to reuse the real user profile. Omit for a throwaway one.

inputs.name: startingUrl
inputs.description: URL the browser opens on launch

inputs.name: chromiumBinary
inputs.description: Custom Chromium-based binary to launch; `browser` still names the target family the engine builds for (chromium-based when none is given).

inputs.name: geckoBinary
inputs.description: Custom Gecko/Firefox binary to launch; `browser` still names the target family the engine builds for (gecko-based when none is given).

inputs.name: host
inputs.description: Bind host, default 127.0.0.1. Use 0.0.0.0 in Docker or devcontainers.

inputs.name: publicHost
inputs.description: Host the browser dials for HMR and reload when it differs from the bind host

inputs.name: extensions
inputs.description: Extra extension paths or store URLs to load alongside the project

inputs.name: headless
inputs.description: false opens a browser window the person can see, overriding EXTENSION_HEADLESS and any --headless in EXTENSION_BROWSER_FLAGS for this session only; pass it when the person wants to watch or try the extension. true forces headless. Omit to inherit the environment (headless when EXTENSION_HEADLESS=1 or EXTENSION_BROWSER_FLAGS carries --headless).

tools.name: extension_stop
tools.description: Stop a session that extension_dev or extension_start is running: terminate the server and the browser it launched, and remove the live-preview carrier if extension_dev placed one. The answer names the server pid and the browser pid the launcher recorded, each with whether it is gone (serverGone, browserGone), so a "close its browser" ask is settled by this answer with no process check by hand. This covers extension_start build:false too, which the registry records as a preview session. Call it when you are done verifying, so sessions do not accumulate.
tools.gate: a live dev or start session
tools.samplePrompt: Stop the running session and close its browser

inputs.name: projectPath
inputs.description: Extension project root

inputs.name: browser
inputs.description: Browser of the session to stop. Only that browser's server and browser processes are ended; a session the same project runs for another browser keeps running. Defaults to the single live session for this project rather than assuming chrome; when the project runs sessions for more than one browser, the call is refused with the list instead of stopping one.

inputs.name: all
inputs.description: Stop every known session across projects and browsers, found from this server's registry AND the on-disk markers written by this server or by servers that are no longer running, so it still works after an MCP restart. Because it crosses projects, a call with no projectPath whose sessions span more than one project answers confirm-required with every session it would end grouped by project (wouldStop) and stops nothing until called again with confirm: true; projectPath beside it scopes the stop to that one project's sessions and carrier with no confirmation, and sessions that all belong to one project need none either. browser is ignored. A marker owned by another MCP server that is still running is left alone and listed under skippedForeign (foreign on a confirm-required answer) unless includeOtherServers is true. It also takes back every live-preview carrier still recorded on this machine, including one in a project whose session was never stopped.

inputs.name: confirm
inputs.description: With all: true and no projectPath, end every session the confirm-required answer listed, across projects. Without it, a stop that would cross projects only lists what it would end.

inputs.name: includeOtherServers
inputs.description: With all: true, also stop sessions whose markers belong to another MCP server that is still running (the markers sit in a per-user directory every server shares). Off by default, since those sessions are someone else's.

tools.name: extension_storage
tools.description: Read or write chrome.storage in a running extension. Every call runs in the extension's background (the engine honors no context), so it proves nothing about what a content script or page can read. A set is read back and the answer says whether the stored value and its type match. Rides the dev session's control channel, on unless extension_dev was called with allowControl:false. One key per call.
tools.gate: a dev session, which carries control unless started with allowControl: false
tools.samplePrompt: Read chrome.storage.local and set settings.theme to dark

inputs.name: projectPath
inputs.description: Extension project root (needs a live dev session)

inputs.name: action
inputs.description: get reads a key (or the whole area); set writes a key

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Key to get or set

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Value to set (any JSON value); action=set needs value or valueJson. Some clients send null as the text "null" and an empty string as the two characters ""; both are refused here as ambiguous, so pass valueJson for them.

inputs.name: valueJson
inputs.description: The value to set as JSON text, parsed by this server so its type survives any client: "null" stores null, "\"\"" an empty string, "0", "false", "[1,2]" and "{\"a\":1}" their own types. Pass value or valueJson, not both.

inputs.name: browser
inputs.description: Session browser; defaults to this project's live session. Required when the project runs sessions for more than one browser: the call is refused with the list rather than picking one.

inputs.name: timeout
inputs.description: Command timeout in ms. When omitted, the default depends on the route: 30000 through the dev session's control channel, 10000 over the Firefox debugger protocol, and 15000 per command over the Chromium debug port.

tools.name: extension_submit
tools.description: Submit a built extension to a store's review through extension.dev, which holds the store credentials and runs the upload (Chrome Web Store, Firefox AMO, Edge Add-ons, App Store for Safari), and run the store steps around it: action preflight, status, sync-listing, configure-store, publish, release (Safari), cancel and rollout. It records a submission and answers what the platform recorded in value.outcome and every link it touched in value.links, waiting up to waitSeconds for the record and answering submit-dispatched until it confirms; submitted-partially names the stores not recorded, and submit-unconfirmed means no usable answer came back, so read extension_release_status before submitting again. Not for sharing, deploying or sending a link (extension_publish) or a local zip (extension_build). It defaults to a dry run that dispatches nothing; dryRun:false submits, which needs a token issued by a workspace owner and a workspace owner's approval of that exact submission, every time, and is irreversible. Submissions land least public: Chrome and Edge as drafts and Safari as a TestFlight build, each entering review only through action:'publish'; Firefox unlisted unless the project saved a release channel. A Firefox upload carries the source repository at the built commit when the Firefox store setting Source archive says so. The project comes from your stored login (extension_auth; tokens live 7 days); project picks one of several logins. Every answer carries value.trackUrl, the console page for it, and value.nextStep {kind, say, url}, what to do or say next.
tools.gate: the server started with --features=local,platform, and a login; dryRun: false, cancel, rollout, release, publish, sync-listing and configure-store need a workspace owner's approval
tools.samplePrompt: Dry run a Chrome and Firefox store submission of the latest build

inputs.name: action
inputs.description: submit (the default) sends buildSha to every store in browsers: Chrome and Edge upload a draft that is not published and does not enter review, even for an item that is already live; Firefox uploads to the unlisted channel whenever the project has no saved release channel (AMO is read only as a guard: an add-on AMO already lists, with no saved channel, is refused before upload, because an unlisted upload of a listed add-on burns the version number) and signs it for self distribution; Safari uploads to App Store Connect and stops at the TestFlight draft; no store's API sets listing visibility, and a store that only uploaded is recorded as 'Uploaded, not public', never as live. A store whose review of another version holds the act answers submit-queued: the platform queued it with the approval bound to it and sends it on its own when that review ends; value.queued names the store's own word and when the platform last checked, nothing is submitted again, and extension_release_status include:['stores'] follows it. status reads, for each store in browsers (default every configured store), the store's own state for the newest version and writes nothing: value.stores [{store, submissionId, version, buildNumber, status, state, readAt, source, releaseType, nextStep}] from the same records as extension_release_status include:['stores'], where state is the store's own word (Apple's App Store version state for Safari) and source where it was read (poll, publish-answer, run, inferred, hand); nextStep is watch while Apple reviews the version and release once Apple reads PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE, and null for a word nothing read from the store; with waitSeconds it first asks for a store check of those stores and answers once it lands (value.refreshWait), so a fresh Apple state takes one call. preflight reads each store's readiness for browsers and writes nothing: the failing checks with what to fix (never a secret value or a secret's name); with projectPath, which failing listing checks the local STORE.md and the built icons already cover (a missing privacy policy URL names the STORE.md line to add); and the store connection: store-not-connected with value.connectUrl, store-connection-failed with the reason, store-item-not-linked with value.linkItemUrl, value.newItemUrl and value.packageUrl, each with the sentences to say in value.sayToPerson (hint and value.nextStep.say point at it, so the signed package link is said once), and the store's own page in value.itemUrl as information only. For Chrome every field only the item's dashboard holds (description, category, language, icon, screenshots, single purpose, permission justifications, remote code, data usage, privacy policy URL, visibility, test instructions) reads unknown with its tab and value.dashboardUrl, never have from STORE.md; the visibility check compares STORE.md's `- Visibility:` (public, unlisted or private; unlisted when absent; written under `## Chrome Web Store`, at the top of the section or under any of its sub-headings) with the Public a new item starts at, and the host check names every content script match and host permission of the built Chrome package no justification bullet covers (a bullet keyed by the pattern, `- *://*/*: <reason>`, or whose reason names it), a localhost or loopback match flagged as a review risk; before the first sync-listing a Chrome row or check that reads the listing record says what STORE.md carries and that it is not synced yet, never that the file is empty. The Chrome preflight also reads Google's own rules from the built package and from the item (fetchStatus): Manifest V3 only, the 128 px icon in the package, the manifest name (75 characters) and description (132), a version above the one Chrome holds, a page that loads a script from outside the package, a missing privacy policy URL on a package that reaches user data, the staged rollout rules (an already-published item, one partial rollout at a time, 100% after a takedown or warning), and a review or upload Chrome is still running; these answer beside the checks as value.storePreflight.<store> {act, blocking, warnings, checks, lock, approval, nextVersion}, where checks carries one row per id in blocking and warnings with its label, expected, actual and message (an id the platform named with no row says so in its actual), the same shape for Chrome and Edge, where a review or upload Chrome is still running is a check with status locked (chrome.review_in_progress, chrome.upload_in_progress) carrying lock {kind, clearsWhen, storeWord, readAt}, a store state that clears by itself and that the platform queues the act on instead of failing it, inFlight names the package Chrome holds in review and approval is the sentence the owner approves. Each store's requirements and bringList list only the rows not on file and count the rest in onFile, so four stores answer in a few KB; detail: true, or the stores and requirement ids it names, answers those rows in full. A preflight with failing checks answers nextStep null, and one whose requirements list reads readyForReview false never answers a submit step: an Edge product never submitted in Partner Center answers the product page as a dashboard step, naming configure-store with storeSettings {firstSubmitted: true} as the write that records it once the owner did. For Edge the platform's report also carries edgePreflight: every rule from Microsoft's own pages as a check {id, severity blocking or warn, lock?} (compressed files and the manifest inside the package, the version against the one the store serves, the first submission, a draft with nothing new, and what Partner Center's listing pages flag: description length, screenshot sizes and count, search-term limits, notes for certification), the review in flight, and edgePreflight.approval, the sentence the approval shows, naming what the act does to what is in flight; a check with lock is a review Partner Center is still running, which clears by itself. sync-listing fills the extension.dev store listing for browsers from projectPath's STORE.md (title, summary, description, category, license, support email, homepage URL, search terms, privacy policy URL, single purpose, permission justifications, reviewer, release and certification notes; a trailing parenthetical note on a category, license, support email or homepage line stays out of the value), the 128 px icon of the build the store receives and the screenshots named, written at once under the owner's own token (listing-synced), and answers what changed and what the listing still lacks; the icon is read from the completed platform build of the commit projectPath has checked out (or the build useBuild names), falling back with no such build to the local dist/<browser> only when its icon matches the source manifest's icon, else to the source icon, and a dist older than the source icon is withheld with the sentence to say (run a build, or pass useBuild), its store answering icon-stale rather than unchanged; each store's row names where its icon came from in value.stores.<store>.icon (build with its sha, dist, or source), and value.iconSource says whether a platform build was used or why not (its build still running per its own record, never pushed, or no git commit), the list's lag never hiding a completed build since the commit's own record is read; Chrome's API cannot write or read any listing field, so a Chrome sync is a record only: its row reads recorded with value.stores.chrome.pasteInDashboard (every field the item's dashboard alone takes, with its tab, Store listing, Privacy, Distribution or Test instructions, the STORE.md line to paste from, and the dashboard address), and a sync of Chrome alone answers listing-recorded, never listing-synced; when the platform still asks for an approval, the first call answers approval-required with the change as the platform computed it and a second call with browsers:[store] and that approvalId writes it once. publish (alias review) with browsers:['chrome'] sends the newest Chrome draft, or the submissionId named, to Chrome's review (while Chrome reviews another package the approval says so, PENDING_REVIEW with the package and the read date, and that this publish waits for that review, which nothing here withdraws; a draft upload meanwhile lands beside the reviewed package without entering review), with browsers:['edge'] the newest Edge Add-ons draft to Edge's certification review (while Partner Center is still reviewing an earlier submission its Publish API answers InProgressSubmission: Can't publish extension as your extension submission is in progress. Please try again later., so a publish the preflight reads as locked is queued behind that review, never failed, and never cancels it; an Edge upload while a submission is in certification review replaces the draft package only and touches no review), and with browsers:['safari'] the App Store version holding the newest TestFlight build, or the build buildNumber names, to Apple's App Review (one review submission for the version; the act creates the version holding the build when none does, set to manual release, so Apple's approval does not put it on sale; a withdrawn or lower build than a newer draft is refused as SAFARI_NEWER_BUILD; another version Apple already holds WAITING_FOR_REVIEW, IN_REVIEW or READY_FOR_REVIEW answers SAFARI_VERSION_IN_REVIEW before any approval, naming the withdrawal that clears it, and the preflight names the same version as a lock on its store.safari_app_review_lock check; a build Apple is still processing or Apple's own refusal per field is answered as the reason; the release mode of a version the owner made is kept): approval-required first, then in-review with value.trackUrl once the record carries the store's own state for the draft in outcome.storeState, read after the act (outcome.liveState is what the store serves meanwhile, never the draft's state), and publish-dispatched until then even when the run finished; with no store connected or no item linked it answers store-not-connected or store-item-not-linked before anyone is asked. An Edge submission whose package carries a compressed file (.zip, .gz, .tgz, .tar, .br, .bz2, .xz, .7z, .rar, .jar, .crx, .xpi, or gzip bytes under any name), which Partner Center refuses in an extension package, answers package-refused with value.files and the build page in value.trackUrl before any approval; the fix is in the build (Tesseract .traineddata ships uncompressed with gzip: false), never in a file this server rewrites. cancel withdraws a submission from review (store, default chrome; submissionId from extension_release_status); with store 'safari' it removes the App Store version from Apple's App Review (refused before any approval when the record says nothing is in review; canceled once the record reads draft, with Apple's version state, DEVELOPER_REJECTED, in outcome.storeState, and the build stays on TestFlight) and rollout raises the Chrome staged rollout to deployPercentage, which Chrome never lets drop again; both need a workspace owner's approval of the exact act and answer approval-required, or a refusal with the reason before anyone is asked. release with browsers:['safari'] (or store 'safari') puts the App Store version Apple approved under manual release on sale, the one App Store Connect holds in PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE unless submissionId or buildNumber names another: approval-required first, the platform's sentence naming the extension, the version and the build and that the platform cannot pull it back; refused before any approval, naming Apple's state, when no version is pending developer release (SAFARI_NOT_PENDING_RELEASE: WAITING_FOR_REVIEW, IN_REVIEW, READY_FOR_SALE), when the version releases automatically after approval (SAFARI_RELEASE_NOT_MANUAL) or when the store is not connected; then release-dispatched until the record confirms, released with Apple's state in outcome.storeState, or release-failed with Apple's words. configure-store changes one store's settings (store, and storeSettings with only what changes: enabled, submissionMode among the store's own mode ids, the store's listing id, the Safari bundleId, the Edge firstSubmitted (the owner's word that the product was submitted once in Partner Center) and storeUrl (the Edge Add-ons listing URL, which names the crx id), and for Firefox sourceArchive and releaseChannel) at once under the owner's own token, the same as extension_builds configure: store-configured answers what changed, the console store settings page in value.trackUrl and preflight as nextStep; a listed or public submission mode changes who can find the extension, so it answers approval-required first with the change as the platform computed it, and a second call with that approvalId applies it once; a storeSettings key that names a credential answers credentials-console-only before anything is sent, with the console connect page in value.connectUrl and the form's own field labels, since store credentials never pass through this server. Recorded statuses (submitted, in-review, canceled, rolled-out, released, listing-synced, listing-recorded) come only with outcome.recorded true; a record that reads failed answers submit-failed or publish-failed; a refusal whose value.approvalRefunded is true keeps its approvalId for the next call.

inputs.name: project
inputs.description: Which stored login to use, as '<workspace>/<project>' (or a project slug that matches one login), when extension_auth has signed in to more than one project on this machine. Omitted, the login this server resolved first is used, after EXTENSION_DEV_TOKEN when that is set, and a login made elsewhere on this machine does not move it. Named, it outranks EXTENSION_DEV_TOKEN. extension_auth (action: status) lists the stored logins.

inputs.name: browsers
inputs.description: Stores to act on: chrome, firefox, edge, safari. A submit takes several; so does publish (chrome, edge, safari, with buildSha) and sync-listing, under one approval per version with one line per store, and the answer's value.lines says per store whether its line ran, was queued, given back or left out.

inputs.name: buildSha
inputs.description: The built commit SHA to submit. It needs a completed build in the project's build index; an unknown sha is rejected.

inputs.name: version
inputs.description: Version label for the submission record (optional).

inputs.name: dryRun
inputs.description: true (the default) rehearses and dispatches nothing: the platform verifies the token and project, finds the store workflow, reads the build from its index and each store's connection record, and answers one value.verdict (ready, not-checked, platform-refused, or the blocking state store-not-connected, store-connection-failed, store-item-not-linked, store-not-configured or store-unhealthy) with value.nextStep and value.trackUrl; it does not run the owner gate, the approval, the build quota, the dispatch pause or the submission-mode check, which the real run does first. false submits: it reads the store connection and refuses before any approval when the store is not ready, needs a token issued by a workspace owner and that owner's approval of this exact submission, dispatches the store workflow, and a Chrome or Edge upload from here stops at the draft under the default modes (Chrome draft-until-public, Edge draft), while a mode saved in the console store settings is honored whoever saved it: Chrome public or staged and Edge review send the upload on to review, and the approval says so (preflight answers the saved mode under value.stores.<store>.submissionMode, extension_release_status under config.submissionMode). Store credentials are never arguments, and no local file is uploaded.

inputs.name: projectPath
inputs.description: Path to the extension project root. A submit and a preflight read it only for the local STORE.md advisory, and nothing local is uploaded; without it a submit's check falls back to the server's working directory. sync-listing requires it and sends the listing text parsed from its STORE.md, the 128 px icon of the build the store receives (the platform build of its checked out commit, else its dist when current, else its source icon) and the screenshots named, nothing else.

inputs.name: approvalId
inputs.description: The approval handle returned by a prior approval-required response for a real submission, a publish, a cancel, a rollout, a release, or a sync-listing or configure-store the platform asked an approval for (a listed or public submission mode). A real submission (dryRun:false) is irreversible and needs a workspace owner's approval every time: call once without this to get an approval id and URL, have a human approve at extension.dev, then call again with the same id. A dry run never needs it. An approval for several stores covers every store it lists once each: call again with the same id and browsers limited to the stores that have not run.

inputs.name: screenshots
inputs.description: With sync-listing, up to 5 PNG screenshots inside projectPath (for example written by extension_screenshot) to set as the listing's screenshots. The Chrome Web Store takes 1280x800 or 640x400.

inputs.name: useBuild
inputs.description: With sync-listing, the sha of a completed platform build to take each store's 128 px icon from, in place of the build of the commit projectPath has checked out; extension_builds lists the shas, and an unknown or unfinished one is refused before anything is sent.

inputs.name: detail
inputs.description: With preflight: what to answer in full. Omitted, each store answers its failing and warning checks whole, and its requirements and bringList list only the rows not on file (an unknown row as its id, label, status and dashboard tab), counting the rest in onFile, so a four-store preflight stays a few KB. true answers every row with its format, how and docs; a list of stores and requirement ids, such as ["chrome", "safari.subtitle"], answers only those in full.

inputs.name: api
inputs.description: Platform base URL (default EXTENSION_DEV_API_URL, else https://www.extension.dev)

inputs.name: store
inputs.description: With cancel or rollout, the store (default chrome, the one store that supports both); with release, safari (the default and the only store with a manual release); with configure-store, the store whose settings change (required).

inputs.name: storeSettings
inputs.description: With configure-store, only the settings that change for store: enabled (boolean: whether the platform submits to this store at all), submissionMode (the store's own mode id: chrome draft-until-public, draft, public or staged; edge draft or review; firefox unlisted or listed; safari draft; dry-run on any store rehearses without uploading), the store's listing id (chromeItemId, edgeProductId, firefoxAddonGuid or appStoreId, a plain write checked in the store's own terms), for Safari bundleId (the project's reverse-DNS bundle identifier, a plain write), for Edge firstSubmitted (true once the product was submitted once in Partner Center, a plain owner write) and storeUrl (the Edge Add-ons listing URL carrying the crx id, a plain owner write), and for Firefox sourceArchive (repository attaches the source repository at the built commit, which Mozilla requires for a bundled build; none sends nothing) and releaseChannel (listed or unlisted, the same write as submissionMode). Never a credential, a publisher id or another store's URL: those stay in the console.

inputs.name: submissionId
inputs.description: With cancel, the platform's id of the submission to withdraw; with publish, the draft to send to review (default the newest draft of that store); with release, the Safari submission whose App Store version to release (default the one Apple holds in PENDING_DEVELOPER_RELEASE). From extension_release_status include:['stores'].

inputs.name: buildNumber
inputs.description: With publish or release and browsers ['safari'], the TestFlight build number Apple shows (extension_release_status include:['stores'] lists each Safari submission's build) to send to App Review, in place of submissionId; omitted, the newest TestFlight build on record is sent. A number no submission carries answers publish-refused with value.knownBuildNumbers, a withdrawn or lower build than a newer draft answers SAFARI_NEWER_BUILD, and the approval names the build: 'Send App Store version 0.2.0 with TestFlight build 13 to Apple's App Review'.

inputs.name: deployPercentage
inputs.description: With rollout, the share of users to raise the staged rollout to: a whole number from 1 to 100, above the current one.

inputs.name: waitSeconds
inputs.description: How long, in seconds, this call waits for the platform's own record to show the act's result before answering: 0 to 600, default 180. 0 reads the record once and answers at once. When the bound passes first, the status is <act>-dispatched with value.outcome.recorded false, and the hint names the read that confirms it later. A read the platform does not answer (a timeout, a refused connection, a 429 or a 5xx) is retried after retryAfterSeconds while the bound lasts, and only when the bound is spent on such reads does value.outcome.readProblem name them with their count. With approvalId, a call that names waitSeconds also waits for an approval nobody has decided yet: it polls the approval every retryAfterSeconds up to the bound, and once a person approves it goes straight on to the act and the record wait in the same call, with what is left of the bound.

tools.name: extension_templates
tools.description: Browse the extension.dev template catalog. Pass action:'list' (the default) to search and filter it and get metadata per template. Pass action:'source' with a `slug` to read one template's files, for learning a pattern before building something similar. Read `framework` as the UI framework only, never the language: TypeScript and JavaScript templates live under slugs ('typescript', 'content-typescript'), shadcn is a React variant ('sidebar-shadcn'), and provider AIs carry the 'ai' tag ('ai-chatgpt', 'ai-claude'). Reach those through query, tags or slug.
tools.gate: none
tools.samplePrompt: Which templates have a side panel? Show me the source of the best one

inputs.name: slug
inputs.description: source: which template to read (e.g. 'ai-claude', 'content-react'). Required for source.

inputs.name: files
inputs.description: source: paths to read (e.g. ['src/manifest.json']). Omit for the file listing.

inputs.name: query
inputs.description: list: keyword search over slug, description, tags and useCases. Ranks by word matches, so a natural phrase works.

inputs.name: surface
inputs.description: list: filter by surface. For a popup/action starter use query:'action', not a surface.

inputs.name: framework
inputs.description: list: UI framework filter (empty string = vanilla JS).

inputs.name: tags
inputs.description: list: filter by tags, e.g. ['ai', 'chat'].

inputs.name: featured
inputs.description: list: only featured templates.

tools.name: extension_theme_verify
tools.description: Verify a Chrome theme manifest before it ships. This settles the four-leg WYSIWYG contract (app-shows == manifest-says == chrome-paints, plus chrome-accepts) as far as is possible headless: it derives every color current Chrome would paint from the manifest through the transcribed Chromium resolver, and classifies each problem as D1 fabrication, D3 parity gap, or D4 acceptance gap (keys Chrome silently discards: dead legacy, incognito, unknown, out-of-range). It verifies only, and never authors or mutates a theme. The app-rendered and real-pixel legs need a browser, so they come back as needsAttended with the step that settles each one (the theme editor at themes.extension.dev, and a dev session in Chrome), never as passed.
tools.gate: none
tools.samplePrompt: Does this theme manifest paint the colors it declares?

inputs.name: manifest
inputs.description: The Chrome theme manifest object (with a `theme` block). Pass this or manifestPath.

inputs.name: manifestPath
inputs.description: Path to a theme manifest.json (or a { manifest } seed wrapper). Read in place of the inline manifest.

tools.name: extension_wait
tools.description: Wait for a running dev or start session to be ready, or for a rebuild after a source edit (for: "rebuild"). Call it for a session started with wait:false, after an extension_dev answer whose ready.status was not "ready", and for a build-only (noBrowser) session, which answers as soon as the compile lands; an extension_dev answer with ready.status "ready" already carries this result, so there is nothing left to wait for. It polls the ready.json contract and reports compiled, browserAttached and guestLoaded (the browser's own target list shows your extension, the trustworthy load signal; null when it could not be checked), every answer carries budgetMs and elapsedMs, and on status 'timeout' call again to keep waiting on the same contract. Every ready answer carries the ports the session bound: port (the dev server), controlPort (the control channel) and cdpPort (Chromium) or rdpPort (Gecko), or debugPortNote when the session opened no debug port, so a question about ports is answered here without a shell. The reload stamp a rebuild wait reads (reloadedAt) needs Extension.js 4.1.34 or later; a project on an older engine gets a brief watch for the background to reconnect instead, answering reattached, still-detached or not-stamped. Not for a condition in the page (a model loading, an element appearing): that is extension_eval with until. Never sleep or tail the session log in a shell to wait. A browser that is running while the extension's background went idle answers status "background-asleep" with how to wake it, not "browser-gone"; a Safari WebDriver session that Safari ended answers "webdriver-session-ended" with the restart that opens a new one.
tools.gate: a live dev or start session
tools.samplePrompt: Wait until the dev session is ready, then tell me the ports

inputs.name: projectPath
inputs.description: Extension project root

inputs.name: browser
inputs.description: Session browser; defaults to this project's live session. Required when the project runs sessions for more than one browser: the call is refused with the list rather than picking one.

inputs.name: timeoutMs
inputs.description: Wait budget for this call. Default 45000, clamped to 1000-50000 so one call stays under the client's 60s request timeout. On timeout, call again to keep waiting.

inputs.name: timeout
inputs.description: Deprecated alias of timeoutMs, which wins when both are given.

inputs.name: for
inputs.description: What to wait for. "ready" (the default) waits for the session to be ready. "rebuild" waits for the compile after a source edit: until ready.json's compiledAt moves past its value at call time (or past since), then for the reload: an engine that stamps reloadedAt is waited on until that stamp lands after the new compiledAt and after its value at call time (a stamp older than the compile, such as the previous Safari re-sync, never counts), answering reload.outcome "reloaded" with reloadKind (full, background, content, page or safari-resync) and reloadLabel; an older engine is watched briefly for the background to connect again (reattached, still-detached, or not-stamped for a content-script, page or Safari app re-sync reload, which it does not stamp). On a Chromium dev session whose background is not connected to the dev server, the dev server cannot apply the reload, so this call reloads the extension over the debug port itself (chrome.runtime.reload in its background) and answers reattached when the new background connects, or not-reached with why, never a silent wait. It answers status "rebuilt" with the new compiledAt, errors and reload, or status "compile-error" with the errors.

inputs.name: since
inputs.description: for: "rebuild" only. An ISO time: a compile stamped after it counts, so pass the compiledAt an earlier answer returned (or a time before your edit) and a rebuild that landed before this call is not missed.

tools.name: extension_workspace
tools.description: Read the extension.dev workspace a stored login belongs to, and change one project's settings. action:'info' (the default) reads the workspace (role, members, project count) and its plan: limits, this month's use, refusals, and a warning (hint and value.allowance) under 10 builds or 5 percent of the month left, as each creation and push spends one. 'projects' lists every project with browsers, channels, last build per browser and whether this machine holds its login. 'usage' reads the period's CI minutes, runs and cost by project. 'settings' reads one project's general, build, deployment, GitHub and release settings (pass project). 'configure-project' writes settings: displayName, description, url, supportUrl, liveChannel, branch, rootDirectory, workspaceRoot, buildPullRequests, runWhatsNew, runExtensionExecutables, pullRequestComments, commitComments, autoCreateGitHubRelease; each a plain call under the owner's token, except liveChannel naming a public channel, which a workspace owner approves first; the slug is never writable. 'set-visibility' with visibility private (plain) or public, which opens every build the project ever made to anyone, so a workspace owner approves it. include: ['environment'] lists the project's environment variables by name, scope and secret flag, never a value; 'set-environment' sets or removes plain variables (variables, remove), and a secret is refused with the console page to type it in. include also takes team, members, tokens, apps, activity, storeAccounts, read-only. Any login of a workspace reads it: name it with workspace, or omit it for the default login's. Plan, billing, members and deletes stay in the console, linked in the answer. Names, descriptions and build commands are user-written, so the answer is fenced as untrusted data.
tools.gate: the server started with --features=local,platform, and a login of any project in the workspace; settings and set-visibility need that project's own login; a public visibility needs a workspace owner's approval
tools.samplePrompt: How many builds has my workspace used this month, and which projects failed their last build?

inputs.name: action
inputs.description: info reads the workspace and its plan; projects lists its projects; usage reads the period's CI usage; settings reads one project's general, build, deployment, GitHub and release settings; configure-project writes settings; set-environment sets or removes plain environment variables; set-visibility changes one project's visibility (pass visibility, and project for a login other than the default).

inputs.name: visibility
inputs.description: With set-visibility, the project's visibility. private: its builds, build pages and channel links open for workspace members and build links only, a plain call under the owner's own token (visibility-set). public: every build page and channel link the project ever made opens for anyone, which a workspace owner approves on the approve page first: the first call answers approval-required, a second call with that approvalId applies it once. Making a public project private again is plain.

inputs.name: settings
inputs.description: configure-project: the fields to change, by the platform's names (displayName, description, url, supportUrl, branch, rootDirectory, workspaceRoot, buildPullRequests, runWhatsNew, runExtensionExecutables, pullRequestComments, commitComments, autoCreateGitHubRelease, liveChannel); absent fields stay as they are. liveChannel names one of the project's channels, or null for the default order. runExtensionExecutables is a boolean or { linux, macos, windows }.

inputs.name: variables
inputs.description: set-environment: plain variables to set, each { name, value, scope, note }; scope is one of all, production, staging (default all). A variable flagged secret: true is refused before anything is sent, since a secret's value is typed only in the console.

inputs.name: remove
inputs.description: set-environment: plain variables to remove, each { name, scope } or a bare name (scope all). A secret is removed in the console.

inputs.name: approvalId
inputs.description: The approval id from a prior approval-required answer, once a workspace owner approved it: set-visibility public, or configure-project making a public channel the live channel. Each approval applies its exact change once.

inputs.name: include
inputs.description: Sections to add to the answer, each read-only. team: the login project's members (login, role, joinedAt) and pending invites. members: the workspace's members and pending invites, read with an owner-minted login. tokens: the project's access tokens (id, label, kind, createdAt, expiresAt, issuedBy, revoked; never a value, and no last use, which the platform does not record). apps: the connected apps holding a live grant (name, connectedBy, connectedAt, expiresAt). activity: the 50 newest activity entries, never naming a repository or a workflow run. storeAccounts: the workspace's store accounts (store, connected, connectedAs, connectedAt, checkedAt, healthy; never a key), read with a member's session or an owner-minted login. Each section carries its console page, where every change to it is made.

inputs.name: workspace
inputs.description: Which workspace to read, by slug. Omitted, the workspace of the login project names, else of the default login. Any stored login of this workspace on the server the call targets serves the read.

inputs.name: project
inputs.description: Which stored login to use, as '<workspace>/<project>'. For settings it is also the project read, since a project's settings are read only with its own login. extension_auth (action: status) lists the logins.

inputs.name: api
inputs.description: Platform base URL (default EXTENSION_DEV_API_URL, else https://www.extension.dev)

tools.name: extension_workspace_create
tools.description: Create an extension.dev workspace that does not exist yet, without opening the console. Use it before extension_project_create when the project's workspace is not there: project creation can only target an existing workspace, and this tool is what brings one into existence. Two-phase, like login: the first call returns a code and a URL where a signed-in GitHub user approves creating exactly this workspace and becomes its owner; call again with the returned deviceCode to finish. Check `ownerGithubLogin` in the answer: whoever approved the code owns the workspace. The approval mints a grant that lives minutes, can only create the one named workspace, names no project, and is kept on this machine only while a create's outcome is unknown: then it sits in a file only this user can read, beside the stored logins, so calling again with the same deviceCode reads that outcome with no second approval. Then run extension_project_create against '<workspace>/<project>'.
tools.gate: the server started with --features=local,platform
tools.samplePrompt: Create a workspace called acme on extension.dev

inputs.name: workspace
inputs.description: Slug of the new workspace, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, no slash. It must not exist yet; a personal workspace (the GitHub login) already exists for every signed-in user, so this is for a shared or organization-style workspace.

inputs.name: displayName
inputs.description: Human name for the workspace. Defaults to the slug.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: Short workspace description. Optional.

inputs.name: developerUrl
inputs.description: Public URL for the workspace. Optional.

inputs.name: deviceCode
inputs.description: Resume token from the prior call's `deviceCode`; omit on the first call.

inputs.name: api
inputs.description: Platform base URL (default EXTENSION_DEV_API_URL, else https://www.extension.dev)
